proposal.title: Diagnostic-first test of a shared-matrix polynomial operator against NeuMiss's untied masked recurrence at equal matrix-vector cost
proposal.hypothesis: Under MCAR Gaussian data, replacing NeuMiss's untied per-layer matrices with one shared matrix A and learned per-step scalars c_k should keep excess MSE over the Bayes predictor within 10% of the untied baseline at the same depth and the same number of d-by-d matvecs. This must be shown on fresh covariance draws, and it is claimed only if an oracle pre-training polynomial check first shows a gap that plain Neumann truncation cannot close.
proposal.baseline: NeuMiss as implemented in neumannS0_mlp.py (Neumann.forward), with mlp_depth=0 and residual_connection=True. The recurrence, recovered from the code, uses x zero-imputed and m the missing indicator. h0 = x + m*mu. h_res = x - (1-m)*mu, which is (x-mu) on observed entries and 0 on missing entries because x is 0 there. Step 1: h1 = (h_res S0)⊙(1-m), with no residual added. For k = 2..depth: h_k = (h_{k-1} W_k)⊙(1-m) + h_res. Then h = (h_depth Wc)⊙m + h0, and y = h·beta + b. The matrices are untied: each is a separate registered parameter W_i. The phase argument is unused, so training and inference run the same function and differ only by no_grad. The model has no uncertainty output. Without the residual, the chain keeps only the top-degree product term rather than a series sum. For a fixed mask, the predictor is affine in x.
proposal.operator_delta: Replace the untied matrices {S0, W_2..W_depth} with one shared matrix A plus learned scalars c_1..c_depth. The recurrence becomes h_k = (h_{k-1} A)⊙(1-m) + c_k h_res. The input/output contract is unchanged: (x zero-imputed, m) of shape (n,d) maps to y of shape (n,). Matvec count is unchanged: depth+1 d-by-d products per sample. Everything else is kept as is: mu, Wc, beta, b, initialization, SGD, scheduler and early stopping.

evidence.supports: Iteration matrices are separately allocated, i.e. untied across layers.
Each iteration is a matvec followed by masking to observed coordinates.
Missing coordinates are filled by a mixing matrix, and observed values are passed through via h0.
The phase argument exists but is never used in the body, so inference equals the training forward pass.
The Bayes predictor uses a mask-specific exact inverse; this is the target the truncation approximates.
The raw-mask baseline is affine in the zero-imputed x and the indicators, with no mask-dependent slopes.

assumptions: Source-supported: the Bayes predictor needs Sigma_obs^{-1} for each mask pattern, and NeuMiss masks each iterate to observed coordinates.
Inferred: the untied matrices mostly emulate powers of one matrix, so a shared A with scalar coefficients loses little. This is testable by oracle polynomial fitting.
Inferred: equal matvec count is the right compute match. Parameter count differs (about d^2 versus depth*d^2) and is reported, not matched.
Inferred: for a fixed scalar step eta, the oracle choice A = I - eta*Sigma bounds what the shared form can represent.

data_paths.input: Oracle Sigma and mu from fresh gen_params draws, plus sampled MCAR masks
data_paths.operation: Before any training, compute the best least-squares degree-depth polynomial in (I - eta*Sigma_obs) applied to (x_obs - mu_obs). Compare its relative error to the exact Sigma_obs^{-1} solve against plain truncated Neumann (all c_k=1).
data_paths.output: Per-mask relative solve error and the predicted excess risk of each variant
data_paths.possible_leakage: Eta is tuned with oracle Sigma. Report eta chosen on development covariances only.

data_paths.operation: Train the untied baseline, the shared-plus-scalar delta, ConstantImputedLR and EMLR
data_paths.possible_leakage: Early-stopping validation set: use a split separate from test. Mask-frequency differences can be absorbed by mu and Wc rather than the operator.

proposal.counterexample: Near-diagonal Sigma (small diagonal noise, prop_latent near 0). Here Sigma_obs^{-1} is essentially diagonal, depth 1 suffices, and ConstantImputedLR or plain Neumann matches both variants, so no operator effect is observable. A second failure case is ill-conditioned Sigma_obs, where no degree-depth polynomial approximates the inverse and both variants fail equally.
proposal.matched_control: Same code with c_k fixed to 1 and the shared A kept: plain tied Neumann, with equal matvecs, depth, initialization, optimizer, epochs, seeds and data. A second control is the untied baseline at the same depth.

experiment.development: Fresh gen_params seeds not used by any launch script. d=20, prop_latent in {0.3, 0.7}, MCAR at 0.25, depth in {3, 5}, 5 seeds. Run the oracle polynomial check first.
experiment.heldout: Untouched new seeds, d=40, MCAR at 0.5, and a covariance family with condition number set by new diagonal ranges. Do not reuse launch_simu_perf, depth_effect or architecture outputs.
experiment.metric: Excess MSE over the Bayes predictor, as a median ratio across seeds and covariances of delta to untied. The oracle relative solve error is also reported.
experiment.kill_threshold: Kill if the oracle polynomial improves on plain Neumann solve error by less than 10% on development. Kill if the held-out median excess-MSE ratio (delta/untied) exceeds 1.10. Kill if the delta does not beat the c_k=1 control by at least 5%. Kill if ConstantImputedLR is within 5% of the delta.

proposal.prior_art_difference: There is substantial overlap. Polynomial/Krylov-style and Chebyshev-style accelerated iterations, adaptive depth, spectral stabilization, and tied versus untied unrolled networks are all extensive prior art. NeuMiss_sota may already use shared weights, which is unverified here. The only proposed difference is a pre-training oracle test of scalar-coefficient sharing inside this exact masked recurrence. Novelty is not established.

review.reason:
The baseline transcription matches the code. h0 = x + m*mu and h_res = x - (1-m)*mu. The first step applies S0 and masks with no residual. The loop runs over l_W[1:depth] and adds h_res only when residual_connection is set. The output is matmul(h, Wc)*m + h0, then beta and b. The phase argument is unused. For a fixed mask the predictor is affine in x.

The delta is not an algebraic no-op. A shared A restricts h_depth to a scalar-weighted polynomial in (A restricted to observed coordinates) applied to h_res. This is a real subset of the untied products. Because the mask is applied after every matvec, the oracle A = I - eta*Sigma reproduces polynomials in (I - eta*Sigma_obs), so the oracle gate is well posed. Every input is observable or a learned parameter.

Three control and identifiability issues remain.

(1) The proposed recurrence adds c_1*h_res at step 1, but the baseline adds no residual at step 1. The 'c_k=1' control is therefore not the baseline structure with tying alone. It changes which terms enter the sum. The fix is to set c_1 = 0 (or omit it) so that only tying differs. Otherwise report both variants.

(2) h_depth enters the output only through Wc, so a common scale of all c_k can be absorbed into Wc. Only the ratios c_k/c_1 are identified. The c_k=1 control is then distinguishable only through the relative weights, which is acceptable but should be stated. The same holds for A versus eta in the oracle check.

(3) The oracle polynomial must use a single coefficient vector shared across all masks, as the learned model does. Fitting it per mask overstates what the delta can represent and would make the 10% gate too easy to pass.

The non-inferiority framing (ratio ≤ 1.10 against an untied model that strictly contains the delta) is coherent. The four kill criteria together can falsify the hypothesis cheaply.

evidence.supports: The first iteration uses S0 with no residual addition, unlike the proposed uniform c_k*h_res recurrence.
The residual-bearing steps are 2..depth, using untied matrices.
The residual is conditional and applies only inside the loop.
The iterate reaches the output only through Wc, so a global scale on c_k is absorbable.
The Bayes target uses an exact mask-specific inverse, against which the oracle solve error is measured.
MCAR masks are independent Bernoulli draws, so many distinct masks share one set of coefficients.

review.strongest_counterargument: These control issues may be immaterial. The step-1 residual changes only one low-degree term, and the free Wc scale is harmless. The question of whether scalar-weighted shared powers suffice is also well studied in polynomial and Krylov preconditioning, so the experiment may only confirm known approximation theory inside this specific recurrence rather than add information.
review.required_test: First, on development covariances, run the oracle check numerically. Use A = I - eta*Sigma, with eta chosen on development covariances, and fit one global least-squares coefficient vector c across all sampled MCAR masks. Compare the per-mask relative solve error against all c_k=1, at depth 3 and 5, d=20. If the gain is under 10%, stop. Otherwise, train three models on identical seeds and data: the untied baseline, shared A with c_1=0 (matching the baseline step 1), and shared A with c fixed to 1. Then apply the stated held-out excess-MSE kill thresholds.
